purpose: Define the production gate for Category + Constraint pages so pages are only created, patched, published, indexed, or scaled after mechanism quality, evidence quality, and current product validation are strong enough to support publication.

page_lifecycle_stages.description: A page idea exists, but no page should be created yet unless the mechanism is clear.
page_lifecycle_stages.creation_policy: Do not create the page unless one dominant failure mechanism and its exact trigger are clearly defined.

page_lifecycle_stages.description: A page can exist locally or as a proof page to test template fit.
page_lifecycle_stages.creation_policy: Creation is allowed only for template testing and structure validation.
page_lifecycle_stages.publish_policy: Not publish-ready and should not be intentionally indexed.

page_lifecycle_stages.description: A validation brief exists and claims are being tested.
page_lifecycle_stages.creation_policy: Page can be drafted or patched only if a research brief exists for the exact Category + Constraint thesis.
page_lifecycle_stages.publish_policy: Not publishable until evidence and validation gates pass.

page_lifecycle_stages.description: Old comparison evidence has been classified and weak, adjacent, or mismatched evidence is not allowed as proof.
page_lifecycle_stages.creation_policy: Page work may continue only when reused evidence has been classified.
page_lifecycle_stages.publish_policy: Still blocked until external validation is complete.

page_lifecycle_stages.description: Key tool claims have current product verification and external facts are separated from internal comparison evidence.
page_lifecycle_stages.creation_policy: Patching is allowed to reconcile current product behavior with existing claims.
page_lifecycle_stages.publish_policy: Eligible for publish readiness review, but not automatically publish-ready.

page_lifecycle_stages.description: The page passed all required gates and can be publicly linked and indexed.
page_lifecycle_stages.creation_policy: Creation, patching, publication, and indexing are allowed.

page_lifecycle_stages.description: A page exists but should not be indexed yet.
page_lifecycle_stages.creation_policy: Patching is allowed only to resolve failed gates.
page_lifecycle_stages.publish_policy: Should not be promoted or intentionally indexed.

page_lifecycle_stages.description: The mechanism is too weak, the category is too broad, or the evidence is too thin.
page_lifecycle_stages.creation_policy: Do not create or continue the page without narrowing or replacing the thesis.

requirements: One dominant failure mechanism must anchor the page.
The exact failure trigger must be defined in precise user-facing terms.
Adjacent mechanisms must be explicitly excluded from the page thesis.
Subcategory scope must be clear enough that the page does not drift across neighboring product types.
Every named tool must have a clear reason to be included for the exact mechanism.
Visible survivor and failure groups must remain tight around the mechanism.
No tool may be named only because it is popular or commonly searched.
No tool may appear without evidence classification.
At least 3 total evidence supports must exist for preferred or survivor conclusions.
At least 2 evidence supports must match the exact mechanism rather than an adjacent one.
Comparison evidence must be classified in content/seo/comparison-evidence-audit.json before reuse.
Adjacent evidence cannot be used as proof.
Old comparison pages are legacy evidence only and cannot be treated as default truth.
Current product behavior for named tools must be checked.
Current docs or official sources are preferred for verification.
Claims must be updated if product behavior changed.
External validation overrides old comparison claims when they conflict.
The page must follow the Category + Constraint structure.
The page cannot read like a generic listicle.
No ranking or recommendation language is allowed.
A clear tradeoff or flip condition must be present.
Only publish_ready pages should be intentionally indexed.
template_proof and needs_revision pages must not be submitted to Google Search Console.
Mass index requests for unvalidated pages are not allowed.

publish_readiness_levels.meaning: All required gates passed and the page is safe to publish, promote, and intentionally index.
publish_readiness_levels.allowed_internal_links: Can receive normal internal linking and intentional promotion.
publish_readiness_levels.allowed_sitemap_indexing_behavior: Can be included in sitemap and intentionally indexed.
publish_readiness_levels.next_action: Publish or continue normal distribution and monitoring.

publish_readiness_levels.meaning: The page is structurally useful as a proof page but not ready for production claims.
publish_readiness_levels.allowed_public_status: May exist locally or as a limited proof, but should not be treated as a publish-ready page.
publish_readiness_levels.allowed_internal_links: Internal references allowed only for template evaluation, not broad promotion.
publish_readiness_levels.allowed_sitemap_indexing_behavior: Do not submit to sitemap or intentional indexing workflows.
publish_readiness_levels.next_action: Create or complete a research brief and start mechanism and evidence validation.

publish_readiness_levels.meaning: The thesis is plausible, but current support is incomplete or under-validated.
publish_readiness_levels.allowed_public_status: May exist internally or live with limited exposure, but should not be promoted as validated.
publish_readiness_levels.allowed_internal_links: Allow only restrained internal references needed for internal review.
publish_readiness_levels.allowed_sitemap_indexing_behavior: Avoid intentional indexing and do not submit to Google Search Console.
publish_readiness_levels.next_action: Expand research, tighten mechanism coverage, and complete external validation.

publish_readiness_levels.meaning: The page relies too heavily on weak, adjacent, or legacy evidence that cannot support the claims.
publish_readiness_levels.allowed_public_status: Should not be treated as publish-ready.
publish_readiness_levels.allowed_internal_links: Do not add new promotional internal links until evidence is replaced.
publish_readiness_levels.allowed_sitemap_indexing_behavior: Do not intentionally index or resubmit.
publish_readiness_levels.next_action: Replace weak or adjacent evidence with exact-mechanism support and re-audit evidence.

publish_readiness_levels.meaning: The core thesis may be viable, but the page expression drifts away from the Category + Constraint template.
publish_readiness_levels.allowed_public_status: May remain internal or minimally exposed during revision.
publish_readiness_levels.allowed_internal_links: Avoid broad internal linking until the template fit is corrected.
publish_readiness_levels.allowed_sitemap_indexing_behavior: Do not intentionally index while template violations remain.
publish_readiness_levels.next_action: Revise the page to restore Category + Constraint structure, tradeoff clarity, and non-listicle framing.

publish_readiness_levels.meaning: The mechanism, category scope, or evidence quality is too weak for creation or publication.
publish_readiness_levels.allowed_public_status: Should not be published or promoted.
publish_readiness_levels.allowed_internal_links: No intentional internal promotion beyond internal planning references.
publish_readiness_levels.allowed_sitemap_indexing_behavior: Must not be submitted for indexing.
publish_readiness_levels.next_action: Narrow the thesis or abandon the page until a stronger mechanism and evidence base exist.

notes: Evidence must support the exact failure mechanism, not a nearby workflow benefit.
Evidence quality should be assessed separately from template quality.
Legacy comparison material can inform research, but cannot by itself prove publish readiness.

preferred_sources: Official release or changelog material when relevant
external_validation_rules.source_separation_rule: External product facts must remain distinguishable from internal comparison conclusions.
external_validation_rules.override_rule: When current external validation conflicts with old comparison claims, the external validation wins.
revalidation_triggers: A tool changed relevant product behavior
A core claim depends on an outdated comparison page
A survivor or failure claim cannot be matched to current official behavior

policy: Freeze old comparison pages as legacy evidence rather than default truth.
Classify comparison evidence before reusing it on Category + Constraint pages.
External validation wins over internal comparison logic when claims conflict.
Rewrite, noindex, or redirect decisions should happen only after audit.

template_rules.consistency_rule: Pages may share template structure, but each page must preserve mechanism integrity rather than forcing consistency across mixed failure modes.

rules: Do not submit proof pages until they are publish_ready.
Do not scale pages just because the template exists.
Index pages only after research brief, evidence audit, and external validation are complete.
If a page is live but not publish-ready, mark its status internally and avoid promoting it.
Do not generate 5 to 10 pages until at least 2 pages pass publish_ready.
Future generated pages must come from structured data plus research brief status.
Pages with broad categories or mixed mechanisms require narrowing before creation.
Category-boundary audits are required when a page mixes subcategories.
scale_blockers: Mechanism drift across adjacent failure modes
Broad categories that blur subcategory boundaries
Evidence sets inherited from comparison pages without audit
Template consistency masking weak claim validity

example_page_statuses.reason: Strong thesis and improved survivor claims, but exact comparison evidence remains limited and needs replacement with stronger mechanism-matched support.

example_page_statuses.page: Time Tracking Tools Without Manual Timers
example_page_statuses.reason: The mechanism is strong, but some tool claims still need current external product validation.

example_page_statuses.page: Team Collaboration Tools for Clear Ownership
example_page_statuses.reason: Category boundaries may be too broad, and the mechanism can drift across chat, shared inbox, project management, and issue tracking.
